title: fix(analytics,runtime,types): gate cube auto-inference on object existence; stop the dispatcher boundary returning raw SQL (#3867)
body:
Closes #3867. Takes both recommendations from the issue, and the live check upgraded one of them: what I filed as "未验证能否真的返回行" **is** a confirmed arbitrary-table read.

## What the live server actually did, before this change

Authenticated admin on a stock CRM dev server:

```
POST /api/v1/analytics/query {"cube":"sqlite_master","measures":["count"],"dimensions":["type"]}

200 {"rows":[{"type":"index","count":262},{"type":"table","count":71},{"type":"view","count":1}],
     "sql":"SELECT type AS \"type\", COUNT(*) AS \"count\" FROM \"sqlite_master\" GROUP BY type"}
```

SQLite's internal schema table — never a registered object — read successfully through the analytics endpoint. My issue write-up hedged that the repro only produced a syntax error; that was because I sent a malformed payload shape. With the correct `AnalyticsQuery` shape, **any table the connection can see was readable.**

## ① Cube auto-inference now requires a registered object

`AnalyticsService.ensureCube` infers a minimal Cube when none is registered, with `cube.sql = <the queried name>`. That is the intended "metric over an object" path — an `object-metric` KPI widget queries `crm_account` with no authored Cube — but it accepted *any* string.

Note this was **not** covered by #3770: that gated the protocol's `analyticsQuery`, which is the *degraded fallback*. A deployment with `@objectstack/service-analytics` installed runs the real engine instead (`ctx.replaceService`), which is the path that was exposed.

Inference is gated on the same schema registry the data path consults, via a new optional `AnalyticsServiceConfig.isRegisteredObject` wired in `plugin.ts` from the `data` engine's `getObject` — so "which objects exist" has one answer across `/data` and `/analytics`. Three-way rule:

| Queried name | Behaviour |
|:---|:---|
| A registered Cube | runs untouched — it was authored, its `sql` is whatever it declares |
| Not a Cube, but IS a registered object | auto-infers exactly as before (the KPI path, unchanged) |
| Neither | `CUBE_NOT_FOUND` / 404, raised **before any SQL exists** |

With no probe configured the gate stands down and warns once — the tiering #3770 took for a missing registry. `generateSql` (`/analytics/sql`) is gated too; leaving it open would hand back SQL naming an arbitrary table.

## ② The dispatcher boundary no longer returns `err.message` verbatim

`errorResponseBase` is the single error exit for **every** route the dispatcher plugin mounts — `/analytics`, `/packages`, `/i18n`, `/storage`, `/automation`, `/auth`, `/notifications`, `/mcp`. `@objectstack/rest` has guarded its data routes against driver dumps forever (`mapDataError`); this boundary guarded nothing.

This half is **unconditional** — it holds regardless of whether the cube is valid, which is why it's fixed separately rather than as fallout from ①.

The heuristic moved from `rest-server.ts` into `@objectstack/types` as `looksLikeInternalErrorLeak` (both packages already depend on it), so the two boundaries share one predicate instead of one having a guard and the other none. `mapDataError` behaviour is unchanged. At the dispatcher it applies **only to 5xx** — a 4xx message is a deliberate business/validation answer and must reach the caller intact. Sanitising costs no diagnostics: the untouched error still reaches `errorReporter` through the existing `__obsRecordedError` side-channel.

## ③ Not in the issue — `errorResponseBase` ignored `status`

It read only `err.statusCode`, while domain errors across this codebase carry `status` (and `HttpDispatcher.errorFromThrown` already reads `status` first). So every deliberate 4xx thrown through a dispatcher route rendered as a **500** — including **#3770's own `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`** on the analytics fallback path. Now reads `status` then `statusCode`.

I hit this by accident mid-verification: a half-reverted build left my gate live against a baseline dispatcher, and the 404 came back as a 500. Worth knowing it was there before this PR, on every dispatcher route.

## Verified live, before → after on the same server

| Case | Before | After |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `crm_account` KPI (control) | 200, rows | **200, rows — unchanged** |
| `sqlite_master` count | 200 `{count:334}` | 404 `CUBE_NOT_FOUND` |
| `sqlite_master` grouped by `type` | 200, real rows | 404 `CUBE_NOT_FOUND` |
| malformed payload on a real object | raw SQL in the body | `Internal server error` |
| `/analytics/sql` on `sqlite_master` | ungated | 404 `CUBE_NOT_FOUND` |

## Tests

- `cube-inference-gate.test.ts` (7) — **4 red without ①**. Covers rejection, the registry not being poisoned by a rejected name, the KPI path still inferring, an authored cube never being gated, `generateSql`, and the stand-down tier.
- `dispatcher-plugin.error-envelope.test.ts` (6) — **4 red without ②/③**. Drives the real registered route handler through the real dispatcher.
- `error-leak.test.ts` (17) — both halves of the predicate: catches driver dumps, leaves business messages alone (the `startsWith` anchoring matters — "Cannot **update** this record while it is locked" must not trip it).

`pnpm test` green across the monorepo (132/132 turbo tasks).

**One pre-existing assertion narrowed, flagging it for review:** `analytics-service.test.ts` asserted `logger.warn` was never called *at all*, which the gate's stand-down warning trips. It now asserts against the no-cube-registered message it is actually about — matching how its sibling case already asserts, and keeping the log-level regression it exists to catch.
